answer: An applicant posts a work-bond at the harbor surveyor's anchor post and receives a one-time cipher keyed to that day's tide-gauge reading plus its first attested job hash. For one tidal cycle it publishes a derivation thread on the quay board so peers can recompute the cipher from those inputs. Two neighbors from different custody domains countersign only if the arithmetic matches; each may vouch for one applicant per cycle. Shared device clock skew or a recycled cipher salt slashes both bonds and voids the thread, so a farm needs a fresh in-person reading and a fresh bond for every puppet.
